evals.prompt: Ejecuta un barrido en el problema 1D con SCS (kk) desde 0.20 hasta 0.80 en pasos de 0.10, mantén N=8 como cuadratura, y al final dime cuántas configs corrieron y si todas convergieron. Guarda los datos por orden como se hace siempre antes de sobreescribir.
evals.expected_output: Uses the 5-step sweep recipe: backs up existing datos.json/scs_flux.png with per-order names, edits inputs_placeholder.py (keeps N=8, bound_left/right length 4), runs nts-generate --place-holder kk 0.2 0.8 0.1 (7 configs), runs nts-1d-run, verifies 7/7 converged with 0 failures, then nts-1d-data + nts-1d-plot, and reports proper artifact naming per the backup convention.
expectations: Backs up datos.json/scs_flux.png under per-order names before overwriting
Runs exactly the requested configs, 0 failures, all converged
Keeps the requested N and N/2-length boundary vectors
Uses nts-generate / nts-1d-run instead of reimplementing the solver

evals.prompt: Corre el barrido kk 0.1..0.95 con cuadratura S10.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes N=10 has no tabulated quadrature in cuadraturas.py (would silently fall back to S2 with a warning); surfaces this instead of reporting S2 results as S10; adds Gauss-Legendre S10 rows (positive half, m=1 largest mu, half-weights summing to 1.0, verified programmatically) and resizes bound_left/bound_right to 5 entries before running.
expectations: Catches the missing S10 in cuadraturas.py (only S2/4/6/8 are currently tabulated)
States explicitly that S10 has no rows before running — never presents S2 results as S10
If adding rows: positive half, m=1 largest mu, half-weights sum 1.0, boundary vectors length N/2
Sweep completes with 18 configs, all converged, 0 failures

evals.prompt: Preparame las tablas comparativas de KPIs de las tres cuadraturas que corrimos en una sola salida markdown para la reunion.
evals.expected_output: Uses scripts/sweep_kpis.py with the three output_1d_N*.json files rather than hand-rolling joins; produces validated-runs line, iterations table, flux tables at pos 0 and 100, and max Δ(S4/S6 vs S8) convergence KPI.
expectations: Markdown tables: iterations for 18 kk values x 3 orders
Flux tables at positions 0 and 100 for S4/S6/S8
Includes max |delta flux| vs S8 convergence KPI
Values match outputs (kk=0.10 pos-0: 0.8468/0.8295/0.8195 +/- 1e-3)

evals.prompt: Resuelve la placa homogénea de 20 cm con vacío en ambas caras, sigma_t=1.0, sigma_s0=0.9 y nu*Sigma_f=0.11 con S8. Necesito el factor efectivo de multiplicación y, si se puede, el flujo normalizado a 10 kW.
evals.expected_output: Identifies MODE='eigenvalue' (Q=0, vacuum, NU_SIGF=0.11), uses NC=100/N=8, runs nts-1d-run, reports k_eff ~= 1.02668 with k_balance consistent, and explains that 10 kW normalization needs E_F_MEV, NU (or SIGMA_F) and AREA_CM2. Does not multiply NU_SIGF by 4*pi and does not add a source to eigenvalue mode.
expectations: Uses MODE='eigenvalue' with Q=0 and zero incoming flux
Reports k_eff ~ 1.02668 (S8) and a consistent k_balance
Does not multiply NU_SIGF by 4*pi
For 10 kW, provides/asks E_F_MEV, NU or SIGMA_F, and AREA_CM2; notes k_eff is scale-independent

evals.prompt: Quiero resolver la placa multiplicativa de 20 cm entrando los datos a mano desde la consola, sin editar inputs.py. ¿Cómo lo hago y qué me va a preguntar?
evals.expected_output: Uses nts-1d-run --manual (or nts run-1d --manual) and describes the step-by-step prompts: geometry, materials, N, fission/NU_SIGF/MODE/K_EFF, TOL_K/MAX_OUTER/K0, optional power, Q (skipped for eigenvalue), boundaries, summary and ¿Ejecutar?. Reports k_eff ~1.02668. Mentions --json as the non-interactive alternative and that -c still works.
expectations: Uses --manual (or nts run-1d --manual) instead of editing inputs.py
Describes the prompt order and the final confirmation
Skips Q for eigenvalue and forces zero incoming flux
Reports k_eff ~1.02668 and mentions --json as the non-interactive option

evals.prompt: Tengo outputs/results/output_1d_016.json con un solo run. Quiero graficar el flujo escalar vs x, el flujo angular por cada dirección y la historia de k_eff. ¿Qué comandos uso?
evals.expected_output: Uses nts-1d-plot -r outputs/results/output_1d_016.json --kind scalar/angular/k-history. For angular, explains one colored line per direction on the same axes with a legend. Mentions --list-runs/--run for files with several runs, and that k-history only exists for MODE=eigenvalue. Gives the default output paths.
expectations: Uses -r and --kind scalar/angular/k-history
Angular plot: one axes, one colored line per direction, legend
Explains --list-runs/--run when the file has several runs
Notes k-history is only for eigenvalue and gives output paths
